differences.aspect: Fit to the brief's core fantasy (solo zombie shooting in a bedroom)
differences.design_x: Three options step down the shooting fantasy into walking/dodging; the recommended option 3 'หลบมือซอมบี้ถึงวัคซีน' (Dodge the zombie hands to the vaccine) explicitly says 'ไม่ได้ยิง แต่ต้องอ่านพื้น หลบมือซอมบี้' (no shooting, but read the floor and dodge zombie hands).
differences.design_y: Same trade-off: option 1 'ห้องปิดตาย: หลบก่อนรุ่ง' states 'เครื่องนี้ยิงไม่ได้ จึงให้ความตื่นเต้นจากการอ่านวงเตือนและหลบให้ทันแทน' (this device can't shoot, so excitement comes from reading warning rings and dodging).
differences.evidence: Both sessions honestly convert the shooting request into a dodge/walk mechanic and keep the zombie theme and solo bedroom setting; neither preserves any shooting.

differences.design_x: Recommended option 3 scores players_fit 5 and is justified as answering 'ทั้ง challenge และ sensation' (both challenge and sensation); the dodge of two zombie-hand rings with a time bonus directly trains a skill.
differences.design_y: Recommended option 1 also targets challenge+sensation, but its mechanics describe a 'เส้นทางวงเล็ก 4 ด่าน' (small loop route) with 'ไม่มีคะแนนแข่ง' (no competitive scoring) and 'ใช้ก้าวสั้นและไม่เร่งให้วิ่ง' (short steps, no rushing), which softens the challenge; its own risk list admits the space is below the 3×3 m minimum so exploration feel is limited.
differences.evidence: Options step: Design X option 3 scores_why.players_fit = 'ตอบทั้ง challenge และ sensation' with score 5; Design Y option 1 mechanics = 'ไม่มีคะแนนแข่ง' and risks note the cramped space limits the experience.

differences.aspect: Quality and differentiation of the three options
differences.design_x: Three clearly distinct axes: out-and-back narrative escape (option 1), calm looping diorama tour with no hazards or timer (option 2), zigzag dodge with time bonus (option 3). Option 2 is a genuinely different low-challenge alternative, giving the creator a real choice.
differences.design_y: Three options are all timed escape/dodge games with 4–5 sequential checkpoints, red hazard rings, and a 5-minute timer; they differ mainly in theme dressing (locked room, ruined city tour, fire-escape story). Option 2 still includes hazards and a timer ('จับเวลา 5 นาทีแบบผ่อนคลาย'), so it overlaps heavily with options 1 and 3.
differences.evidence: Options step: Design X option 2 mechanics = 'ไม่มีวงอันตรายและไม่จับเวลา' (no danger rings, no timer) versus Design Y option 2 mechanics = 'วงแดงคือซากตึกถล่ม... จับเวลา 5 นาทีแบบผ่อนคลาย' (red rings are rubble... relaxed 5-minute timer).

differences.aspect: Safety in the real space (bed against wall, 2.2×2.5 m, night)
differences.design_x: Prototype pillars require the route to be safe and clear of the bed; build plan says hazards must be positioned so the player can detour 'without moving toward the bed', walking-only, no jump scares, spawn circle 0.6 m, hazards 0.35 m radius.
differences.design_y: Prototype test questions ask whether the player avoids turning their back to the bed while dodging; build plan says place nothing on the bed, leave 'obvious safe gaps' around both hazards, zombies only around the perimeter, no jump scares, nothing overhead.
differences.evidence: Both sessions address the bed, enforce walking-only, ban jump scares, and keep props small; the level of safety specificity is comparable (Design Y's hazard sizes are slightly smaller, ~0.09–0.10 normalized r in the sketch, Design X's 0.35 m radius, but both leave detour room).

differences.aspect: Specificity and feasibility of the build plan
differences.design_x: Build plan gives exact counts and measurements: exactly two hazards of ~0.35 m radius, 2–4 vignettes, 8–20 small objects total, checkpoints 0.5–1 m apart, 0.6 m spawn circle, palette hex codes, and explicit placement of each hazard between named checkpoints.
differences.design_y: Build plan gives exact checkpoint order and Thai labels, two hazards (one 'broad central', one 'slightly smaller' before checkpoint 3), perimeter zombies and palette, but no object counts, no hazard radius in metres, and no spacing measurements.
differences.evidence: Build plan step: Design X layout_brief contains '0.35 m radius', '8–20 small low-poly objects', '0.5–1 m apart', '0.6 m spawn circle'; Design Y layout_brief contains no numeric sizes or counts beyond 'exactly two red floor hazards'.

differences.aspect: Internal consistency between steps (options → prototype → build plan)
differences.design_x: The chosen option 3's mechanics (4 checkpoints, 2 hazard rings, 5-minute limit, time bonus) carry through the prototype (same checkpoint names, same two hazards, scoring −25/+100/+300) into the build plan unchanged.
differences.design_y: Mostly consistent, but the option 1 mechanics say 'ไม่มีคะแนนแข่ง' (no competitive scoring) while the prototype decisions and build-plan rules introduce a full scoring system (−25 per grab, +100 per checkpoint, +300 finish plus time bonus); also the flow timeline places the final door crossing at 4:35 and auto-end at 5:00, which is fine, but the scoring contradiction between steps is a real drift.
differences.evidence: Design Y options step option 1 mechanics: 'จับเวลา 5 นาที เล่นคนเดียว ไม่มีคะแนนแข่ง' vs prototype decisions: 'เหยียบวงแดงลบ 25 คะแนน... จบให้ 300 คะแนนบวกโบนัสเวลา' and build plan rules with the same scoring. Design X shows no such contradiction.

differences.design_x: Dodge design has a defined skill (read the ring, choose step timing), a time bonus for mastery, and an explicit replay loop ('เล่นซ้ำได้เพื่อทำเวลาและคะแนนให้ดีขึ้น'); flow ends main path at 2:20 leaving buffer in the 5-minute session.
differences.design_y: Similar checkpoint+dodge structure with scoring and a retry invitation, but the loop route with short steps and the option-level statement of no competitive scoring frame it more as a one-shot atmospheric escape; flow uses the full 5 minutes with the climax at 3:20.
differences.evidence: Prototype step: Design X flow t=2:40 'เลือกเล่นซ้ำได้เพื่อทำเวลาและคะแนนให้ดีขึ้น' and option 3 mechanics include 'ให้โบนัสตามเวลา' (time bonus); Design Y option 1 mechanics 'ไม่มีคะแนนแข่ง' and flow t=5:00 auto-end.

differences.design_x: Vaccine-evacuation fantasy: first-aid point, wrecked car, vaccine cabinet, evacuation point; story in build plan ties the props together.
differences.design_y: Last-stand-before-dawn fantasy: radio signal, emergency light, unlock escape, safety door; equally coherent mini-story with a hopeful teal exit.
differences.evidence: Both prototype storyboards and build-plan stories are internally consistent and match their checkpoint labels; neither is clearly stronger.

improvements: Design Y: resolve the scoring contradiction — either keep the option's 'no competitive scoring' promise in the build plan or update the option text so the creator isn't surprised by a points system.
Design Y: add concrete measurements to the build plan (hazard radius in metres, checkpoint spacing, object counts) as Design X does, so the layout can be built and safety-checked without guessing.

Design X: the main path finishes around 2:20 of the 5-minute budget; consider whether the unused time is intentional buffer or whether a third hazard or optional bonus objective would use the session length better.

Both: the brief asked for a shooting game; both sessions could more explicitly acknowledge the gap and offer the creator a clear note on why shooting was dropped and what would be needed to restore it.

Design X: option 2 (calm diorama tour) is a good differentiator but its 5-minute estimate versus a fast walkthrough is flagged as a risk; a rough per-checkpoint dwell time would make it more convincing.
summary: Both sessions honestly convert the unfulfillable 'zombie shooting' brief into a walking/dodging MR game in the same 2.2×2.5 m bedroom, with comparable safety handling. Design X is stronger overall: its three options are genuinely differentiated (narrative escape, calm diorama tour, skill dodge), its recommended option best matches the requested challenge+sensation pair (players_fit 5), its build plan is measurably more specific (hazard radius 0.35 m, 8–20 objects, 0.5–1 m checkpoint spacing, 0.6 m spawn circle), and it is fully consistent from options through prototype to build plan. Design Y's three options are near-identical timed escape-dodge games, and it drifts between steps: option 1 promises 'no competitive scoring' yet the prototype and build plan introduce a full scoring system. Design Y is still coherent and safe, but less decisive and less buildable as written.
why: Design X wins on three concrete, page-visible grounds: (1) option quality — Design X offers a real spread of experiences while Design Y's three options share the same loop, hazards, timer, and structure; (2) specificity — Design X's build plan carries numeric layout constraints a builder can act on, Design Y's does not; (3) consistency — Design Y contradicts itself on scoring between the options step and later steps, while Design X carries identical mechanics, checkpoint names, and scoring through all steps. On the brief's core fantasy, safety, and narrative coherence the two are equivalent, so the verdict rests on differentiation, specificity, and consistency.
x_weaknesses: The recommended dodge game finishes its main path around 2:20–2:40 of the 5-minute session, leaving the time budget underused unless the player replays.
Like Design Y, it drops the requested shooting entirely; the conversion is honest but the creator's original fantasy is only partially served.
Option 2's 5-minute duration is self-flagged as potentially too long if the player finishes the four checkpoints quickly.
y_weaknesses: Internal inconsistency: option 1 mechanics state 'ไม่มีคะแนนแข่ง' (no competitive scoring), but the prototype decisions and build-plan rules add a full scoring system (−25/+100/+300 plus time bonus).
The three options are weakly differentiated — all are timed 4–5 checkpoint escape/dodge routes with red hazard rings, differing mostly in theme skin.
Build plan lacks measurable layout data (no hazard radius in metres, no checkpoint spacing, no object counts), making it harder to build and safety-verify than Design X's plan.

Option 1's own risk list notes the space is below a 3×3 m minimum, highlighting limited movement feel, and the 'no competitive scoring, short calm steps' framing undercuts the requested challenge feeling.
